name: The New Pornographers
label: Matador
lede: It started in 1997 as a side project for a pop songwriter, a country singer, a cryptic poet and a filmmaker on keyboards. Ten albums later, through Matador, Concord and Merge, the New Pornographers are still going.

eras.title: A side project that took three years
eras.text: A.C. Newman had come out of Vancouver's Zumpano, Dan Bejar had just started Destroyer, and Neko Case had a country career of her own. Nobody planned to make this the main band, and the first album took nearly three years to finish.

years.h: A.C. Newman builds a band out of other people's bands
years.p: Newman pulls in [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]], [[Dan Bejar|9f142b12-570e-464d-9cb0-f1d579bb6a66]] of [[Destroyer|61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5]], bassist [[John Collins|17fe13d1-ca12-4e28-a7d5-0deb9f631650]] and filmmaker [[Blaine Thurier|57ec12b3-f6ae-4cb1-bdb2-d53c168adf08]] on keyboards, with Fisher Rose on drums.
years.xp: Newman came out of the Vancouver bands Superconductor and [[Zumpano|52203489-c14f-4e60-8aa4-4691da1c974f]]. The name comes from a Japanese film, The Pornographers, and doubles as a nod to the pop group the New Seekers and to The Pornographers, a song on Destroyer's debut We'll Build Them a Golden Bridge.

years.h: Limblifter's drummer takes over from Fisher Rose
years.p: [[Kurt Dahle|8ebf990e-845f-4abf-a606-1f6cf14f2c23]], also of The Age of Electric, takes the kit and keeps it for fifteen years.

yt: Letter from an Occupant, the official video
years.h: Mass Romantic arrives on Vancouver's Mint Records
years.p: David Carswell and Collins produce the debut, recorded over nearly three years. Entertainment Weekly calls it a perfect pop album.
years.xp:
Newman and Bejar split the songwriting, and Bejar's Breakin' the Law was a Destroyer song first. The closing chorus is credited to the Camp Northstar Kids' Chorus, a joke on the film Meatballs: it's just the band singing.

Pitchfork wrote that it was "the catchiest thing to come out in ages." Metacritic scores it 87. Letter from an Occupant, sung by Case, was the only single, in April 2002.

eras.title: The critics got there first
eras.text: Mass Romantic never charted in Canada or the US, but it won a Juno and made critics' lists, and the first tour sold out despite blown voices and broken gear. Electric Version was the first of their records to come out on Matador in America.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mass Romantic · Wikipedia: The New Pornographers
years.h: A record that never charted wins a Juno
years.p: Mass Romantic takes the Juno for Alternative Album of the Year with no chart placing in Canada or the US. Pitchfork had ranked it No. 9 of 2001.
years.xp: Blender's 2007 list put it at No. 24 among the greatest indie rock albums, and Stereogum later called it one of the greatest power pop albums. Rolling Stone's Douglas Wolk wrote of "forty staggeringly catchy minutes of four-part harmonies and Wall of Sound production."

years.h: A film crew rides along on the Western Canada tour
years.p: Director Reginald Harkema films the 2002 run for Better Off in Bed, a documentary about the band's relationships with each other and with opening act The Gay.

years.h: Matador takes the band to the US with Electric Version
years.p: Mint in Canada and Matador in the US release the second album on May 6. Rolling Stone later puts it at No. 79 among the best albums of the 2000s.
years.xp: Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll placed each of the band's first four albums in its top 40. From 2000 to 2006, either a New Pornographers album or a solo record by a member made that top 40 every year.

years.h: Todd Fancey joins on guitar
years.p: A solo artist in his own right, [[Todd Fancey|5f1c3469-cbed-4606-b656-a1cd30b2571c]] becomes guitarist and backing vocalist, and stays.

years.src: Wikipedia: Better Off in Bed · Wikipedia: The New Pornographers
years.h: The band's lawyers step in on its own tour film
years.p: Better Off in Bed premieres at the Whistler Film Festival on December 4. The band didn't like its portrayal and stopped a wider release.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports the band was uncomfortable that the film probed their personal lives rather than concentrating on the tour, and that their lawyers intervened to prevent a wider commercial release after the festival run.

eras.title: Peak years, with family on keyboards
eras.text: Their biggest sales came while the members' solo careers took off too. Case's calendar got too full for touring, and the fix was family: a young Victoria singer who turned out to be Newman's niece.

years.cap: On stage at the Belly Up, Solana Beach
years.h: Newman's niece fills in for Neko Case, then stays
years.p: [[Kathryn Calder|aeb6221d-f90d-4f45-a36a-eccd09b749fd]] of [[Immaculate Machine|9f01b9ea-162d-47f5-93b1-3f6a3aeb4b24]] covers Case's touring dates and becomes a full member.
years.xp: Calder's mother was adopted as a baby and later found her birth family, which included Carl Newman. Calder learned he was her uncle as a teenager, while she was already in a band. In her words: "My mom was adopted as a baby and about ten years ago she found her birth family and Carl is in her birth family."

years.cap: On stage, October 2005, on the Twin Cinema tour
years.h: Pitchfork gives Twin Cinema a 9.0
years.p: Mint and Matador release it August 23. It reaches No. 44 on the Billboard 200 and tops PopMatters' list of 2005, and by 2010 it had sold 138,000 copies in the US.
years.xp: Recorded from November 2004 to April 2005 and produced by Collins, David Carswell, Newman and Dahle. Metacritic scores it 85; NME was cooler at 5 out of 10. It was shortlisted for the 2006 Polaris Music Prize, and Pitchfork later placed it at No. 150 on its top 200 albums of the 2000s.

years.h: Case's own record debuts at No. 54
years.p: [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]]'s Fox Confessor Brings the Flood debuts at No. 54 on the Billboard 200. Her 2009 album Middle Cyclone reaches No. 3.

years.cap: John Collins, A.C. Newman and Kathryn Calder on stage, October 2007
years.src: Wikipedia: Challengers · Wikipedia: The New Pornographers
years.h: Calder takes her first lead vocal on Challengers
years.p: Made at the Seaside Lounge in Brooklyn and released by Matador, Challengers debuts at No. 34. Calder sings lead on Failsafe.
years.xp:
Phil Palazzolo, Collins and Newman produced it, recorded across 2006 and 2007. It sold about 20,000 copies in its first week and 109,000 in the US by 2010.

Critics were warm but not wild: 74 on Metacritic, an A- from The A.V. Club, 6.0 from Pitchfork. Myriad Harbour landed at No. 79 on Rolling Stone's list of the best songs of 2007.

years.cap: On stage, July 26, 2010, on the Together tour
years.src: Wikipedia: The New Pornographers · Wikipedia: Kathryn Calder
years.h: Together carries a dedication to Calder's mother
years.p: Matador releases it May 4 and it reaches No. 18 in the US. Calder's mother had died of ALS while Calder cared for her.
years.xp: Guests include St. Vincent, Zach Condon of Beirut and Will Sheff of Okkervil River. In Canada it reached No. 14. Calder recorded her own debut solo album while caring for her mother, and paused it after her death.

eras.title: A high-water mark, then two exits
eras.text: After a four-year break, Brill Bruisers became the band's highest-charting album. Then the drummer of fifteen years left, and Bejar, whose songs had always been the wild card, sat out a record.

years.h: After four years off, Brill Bruisers hits No. 13
years.p: A.C. Newman called it a celebration record. It's the band's highest US chart placing and its last album on Matador.
years.xp:
Newman: "After periods of difficulty, I am at a place where nothing in my life is dragging me down and the music reflects that." Metacritic scores it 79.

Case, Bejar, Calder and Amber Webber all sing on it. It was shortlisted for the 2015 Polaris Music Prize, and the singles were Brill Bruisers, War on the East Coast and Dancehall Domine.

years.h: Fifteen years in, Dahle hands over the drums
years.p: Kurt Dahle leaves in mid-2014 and Joe Seiders takes his place.

q: Sometimes we avoided Destroyer, sometimes Destroyer avoided us.
years.h: Whiteout Conditions comes out without a Bejar song
years.p: The band's first album on its own Collected Work imprint through Concord has no Bejar songs. Newman put it down to a Destroyer record Bejar was in the middle of.
years.xp: The album was announced January 26, 2017, ahead of its April 7 release, with the single High Ticket Attractions. Newman said Bejar was in the middle of a Destroyer record, "something we'd narrowly skirted for our whole career."

eras.title: The line-up keeps turning over
eras.text: A violinist joined and left, Bejar came back and left again, and founding keyboardist Blaine Thurier departed. In 2025 an arrest forced the band to drop a drummer and replace his parts on the new record.

years.h: Simi Stone goes from touring player to full member
years.p: The violinist and singer, on the road with the band since 2015, joins formally for the Concord-era album.

years.h: Dan Bejar rejoins as two members leave
years.p: Announcing tours that play whole albums, the band confirms Bejar's return. Founding keyboardist Blaine Thurier and Simi Stone depart.

years.h: Merge Records takes the band on for Continue as a Guest
years.p: A.C. Newman announces the move on January 9. Bejar, billed as a former and possibly future member, gets a co-writing credit on Really Really Light.
years.xp: Press photos for the album confirmed Bejar was out of the touring line-up, though his writing credit stayed.

years.h: The band ends drummer Joe Seiders' employment after an arrest
years.p: Seiders was arrested in California on child pornography charges. The band cut ties with him immediately.
years.xp: In November 2025 the band confirmed it would carry on and tour North America in 2026. Charley Drayton overdubbed new drum parts on the tenth album, and Newman told Rolling Stone he wanted to re-record three earlier albums to remove Seiders' drumming.

years.h: Ten albums in, The Former Site Of
years.p: Merge releases the tenth album, led by the single Votive. Josh Wells of [[Destroyer|61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5]] and [[Black Mountain|4898b9ad-f564-4ff1-9046-b1a16dfd5200]] drums on the tour.
years.xp: The album was announced in January 2026, with Pure Sticker Shock (February 10) and Spooky Action (March 2) following Votive as singles. Jess Nolan joined the touring band on backing vocals and keyboards.
